parameters.content:
## 🧬 SEO Digital Twin — Live Knowledge Graph of a Website

This workflow turns a real website into a queryable database model: every page, its keywords, its named entities, and every link between pages, stored as nodes and edges you can query, visualize, or feed into other tools.

### Pipeline
Website → Crawler (sitemap + HTTP fetch) → n8n (extraction + Claude) → Pages + Keywords + Entities + Links → SEO Knowledge Graph (Postgres) → Digital Twin (queryable model + Slack summary)

### How it works
1. Trigger manually or on a weekly schedule, with every setting centralized in Set - Crawl Config.
2. The sitemap is fetched and parsed into a capped, deduped list of page URLs (same-domain only by default).
3. Loop Over Pages processes one URL at a time: fetch HTML, extract on-page elements, then ask Claude to extract keywords, entities, and topics from the page content.
4. Every page, keyword, entity, and link is written into Postgres as a graph: seo_pages (nodes), seo_keywords / seo_entities (nodes), seo_page_keywords / seo_page_entities / seo_page_links (edges).
5. A Merge node waits for every graph write to finish before releasing the next page, so the database always reflects a consistent crawl state.
6. Once every page is processed, the workflow aggregates the graph into digital-twin stats (page count, keyword count, entity count, internal links, orphan pages) and posts them to Slack.

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n.
2. Add credentials: Postgres (or your graph DB of choice), Anthropic API (header auth, x-api-key), Slack API.
3. Create the tables: seo_pages, seo_keywords, seo_page_keywords, seo_entities, seo_page_entities, seo_page_links (see the field names used in the Postgres nodes' queries).
4. Edit Set - Crawl Config: seedUrl, sitemapUrl, maxPages, sameDomainOnly, anthropicModel, slackChannel.
5. Run the Manual Trigger with a small maxPages value to test end to end before scheduling full crawls.

### Requirements
- A Postgres database (or equivalent relational store) to hold the knowledge graph tables.
- Anthropic API access (Claude) for keyword/entity/topic extraction.
- Slack API access for the completion summary.
- The target site should have a reachable sitemap.xml for best coverage; otherwise the crawl falls back to the seed URL alone.

### How to customize
- Feed discovered internal links back into the crawl queue for true recursive crawling beyond the sitemap.
- Add a vector-embeddings step per page for semantic search over the digital twin.
- Add change-detection (diff against the previous crawl) to flag pages whose keywords/entities shifted between runs.
- Swap Postgres for Neo4j or another native graph database if you want Cypher-style graph queries.

## 1. Trigger, Config & Page Discovery

Manual Trigger - Start Crawl lets you kick off a crawl by hand for testing.

Schedule Trigger - Recrawl Weekly re-runs the whole crawl automatically on a weekly cadence so the digital twin stays current.

Set - Crawl Config centralizes the seed URL, sitemap URL, max pages to crawl, same-domain-only flag, Anthropic model, and Slack channel used everywhere downstream.

HTTP Request - Fetch Sitemap downloads the site's sitemap.xml so the crawler knows every page to visit (continueOnFail, since not every site has one).

JS - Parse Sitemap URLs extracts every <loc> URL from the sitemap, falls back to just the seed URL if no sitemap was found, filters to the same domain when configured, and caps the list to maxPages.

Loop Over Pages processes one page URL at a time so each page is fetched, extracted, and written to the graph before the next one starts.

## 2. Per-Page Fetch & Content Extraction

HTTP Request - Fetch Page HTML downloads the raw HTML for the current page in the loop (continueOnFail so one broken page doesn't stop the crawl).

HTML - Extract Page Elements pulls the title, meta description, H1 tags, visible body text, and every link's href + anchor text out of the HTML using CSS selectors.

JS - Normalize Page Data resolves every link to an absolute URL, classifies each as internal or external against the seed domain, and computes the page's word count.

HTTP Request - Claude: Extract Keywords & Entities sends the page's title, meta description, and body text to Claude and asks for primary/secondary keywords, named entities, and topic categories as structured JSON only.

JS - Parse Keyword & Entity Extraction safely parses that JSON, falling back to empty keyword/entity lists if Claude's response can't be parsed.

JS - Build Graph Records turns the page, its keywords, its entities, and its links into four separate record lists ready to be written as nodes and edges in the knowledge graph.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Writing the Knowledge Graph

parameters.content:
## 3. Writing the SEO Knowledge Graph

Postgres - Upsert Page Node writes/updates this page's row (url, title, meta description, H1, word count) in the seo_pages table.

Split Out - Keywords For Insert turns this page's keyword list into one item per keyword so each can be written as its own graph edge.

Postgres - Upsert Keyword Node & Edge writes each keyword and its page-keyword relevance edge into seo_keywords / seo_page_keywords.

Split Out - Entities For Insert turns this page's entity list into one item per entity so each can be written as its own graph edge.

Postgres - Upsert Entity Node & Edge writes each named entity and its page-entity edge into seo_entities / seo_page_entities.

Split Out - Links For Insert turns this page's outbound links into one item per link so each can be written as its own graph edge.

Postgres - Upsert Link Edge writes each internal/external link as an edge into seo_page_links, which is what turns individual pages into a connected graph.

Merge - Sync Before Next Page waits for all four graph-write branches to finish, then releases the loop to move on to the next page — this keeps the crawl from racing ahead of its own database writes.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Assembling the Digital Twin

parameters.content:
## 4. Assembling the Digital Twin

Postgres - Fetch Digital Twin Stats runs once the whole site has been crawled, aggregating total pages, total unique keywords, total entities, total internal links, and orphan pages (pages nothing links to) from the graph tables.

JS - Build Digital Twin Summary combines those stats with the run config into one summary object.

Slack - Post Digital Twin Summary posts the finished digital twin's size and health stats to Slack, with the Postgres tables (seo_pages, seo_keywords, seo_entities, seo_page_links) standing in as the live, queryable model of the site.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.anthropicModel, max_tokens: 1200, system: "You are an SEO content analyst. Given a web page's title, meta description, and body text, extract: primaryKeywords (3-8 keyword phrases most central to the page, each with a relevanceScore 0-1), secondaryKeywords (up to 10 supporting keyword phrases as plain strings), entities (named people, organizations, products, or places mentioned, each as {name, type}), and topicCategories (up to 5 broad topical categories this page belongs to). Respond with ONLY a JSON object: { primaryKeywords: [{keyword, relevanceScore}], secondaryKeywords: [string], entities: [{name, type}], topicCategories: [string] }. No prose, no markdown fences.", messages: [ { role: "user", content: JSON.stringify({ pageUrl: $json.pageUrl, title: $json.title, metaDescription: $json.metaDescription, bodyText: $json.bodyText }, null, 2) } ] }) }}

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO seo_pages (page_url, title, meta_description, h1, word_count, crawled_at)
VALUES (
  '{{ $json.pageRecord.pageUrl.replace(/'/g, "''") }}',
  '{{ ($json.pageRecord.title || '').replace(/'/g, "''") }}',
  '{{ ($json.pageRecord.metaDescription || '').replace(/'/g, "''") }}',
  '{{ ($json.pageRecord.h1 || '').replace(/'/g, "''") }}',
  {{ $json.pageRecord.wordCount || 0 }},
  '{{ $json.pageRecord.crawledAt }}'
)
ON CONFLICT (page_url) DO UPDATE SET
  title = EXCLUDED.title,
  meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description,
  h1 = EXCLUDED.h1,
  word_count = EXCLUDED.word_count,
  crawled_at = EXCLUDED.crawled_at;

SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seo_pages) AS total_pages,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seo_keywords) AS total_keywords,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seo_entities) AS total_entities,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seo_page_links WHERE is_internal = true) AS total_internal_links,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seo_pages p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM seo_page_links l WHERE l.target_url = p.page_url)) AS orphan_pages;
